# gqrx-sdr

**Graphical SDR receiver — waterfall, demodulators and a bookmark list**

- **Version recorded:** 2.17.6
- **Categories:** `sdr-receivers`
- **Upstream:** <https://gqrx.dk/>

## What it does

A general-purpose SDR receiver with a waterfall display, the usual analogue demodulators, recording, and a remote-control interface other software can drive.

## Why you would want it

It is the receiver most people are pointed at first, it works with anything gr-osmosdr or SoapySDR reaches, and its remote-control interface lets satellite tracking software steer it for Doppler correction.

## Before it will work

A supported receiver and its driver. Audio output through PulseAudio or PipeWire.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profiles:** [`listening`](../profiles/listening.md), [`sdr`](../profiles/sdr.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install gqrx-sdr --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `gqrx-sdr`

## Known problems

Built on GNU Radio, so it inherits GNU Radio's version sensitivity. The apt install this manifest performs is insulated from that in the steady state — the archive rebuilds gqrx-sdr against its own GNU Radio — but a partial upgrade that moves GNU Radio before the rebuilt gqrx-sdr arrives can leave it unable to start until the archive catches up. On Wayland the waterfall can be slow; AHRL's guidance to prefer X11 for ham applications applies here.

## Keeping it current

- probe: apt policy
- strategy: apt_upgrade
